correctness.rationale: For n>=2, real alpha>0 and any smooth strictly convex score, Dirichlet neutrality gives a strictly convex one-coordinate conditional mean. Size-biased beta stochastic ordering rigorously makes its left endpoint exceed the unconditional mean; strict convexity makes its right endpoint exceed the mean. Tail integration then has exactly one interior sign crossing. The quadratic formula follows by an explicit verified beta-density antiderivative. All 4,156 exact rational verifier comparisons passed; finite tests are not the universal proof.

The continuous interpolation from 1/2 to 1/n is a substantive finite-sample generalization, not a minor numerical constant adjustment or a marginal re-tabulation.
